display.title: Pirkei Avos Chapter 2: The Eye That Sees, the Ear That Hears
display.summary_short: Why we learn Pirkei Avos between Pesach and Shavuos, and the Mishnah's three things that keep us humble: an eye that sees, an ear that hears, and a book where all our deeds are written.
display.summary_long: A short Sefirah-time talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that in the days between Pesach and Shavuos we work on improving our character so we will be ready to receive the Torah, and that is why we learn a chapter of Pirkei Avos each week. He recalls last week's lesson: Moshe Rabbeinu, the greatest of all people, stayed humble, a lesson he learned from Har Sinai, the lowest mountain. Then he turns to chapter 2, which teaches the secret of humility: remember three things. There is an eye that sees everything you do, an ear that hears everything you say, so you will never use bad language or tell a lie, and a book, always open before Hashem, where everything you think, say and do is written. Remembering these keeps us doing only what is good in Hashem's eyes.
display.lesson: Remember that Hashem sees what you do, hears what you say and writes it all down, and you will stay humble and do only what is right.
